criteria.text: Sign up with a username and a password
Sign in, which gives a token for the requests that follow
Create an item with a title; it starts not done
List your own items
Mark one of your items done or not done
Delete one of your items
Accounts and items survive a restart of the service
JSON over HTTP. An item is {"id": <integer>, "title": <string>, "done": <boolean>}
POST /signup with {"username": ..., "password": ...} answers 201 with {"username": ...}, or 409 when the username is taken. A missing or empty username or password is refused with 400 or 422
POST /signin with {"username": ..., "password": ...} answers 200 with {"token": <string>}, or 401 when they do not match an account
Every request below sends the header Authorization: Bearer <token>; without a valid token it answers 401
POST /items with {"title": ...} answers 201 with the item. A missing or empty title is refused with 400 or 422, and nothing is stored
GET /items answers 200 with a JSON array of the signed-in person's items only
PATCH /items/{id} with {"done": true|false} answers 200 with the item, or 404 when it is not one of the signed-in person's items
DELETE /items/{id} answers 204, or 404 when it is not one of the signed-in person's items
GET /health answers 200 without a token

The project directory has a start.sh that starts the service on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the PORT environment variable, keeping its data under the directory in the DATA_DIR environment variable. Nothing else is set in its environment: any secret it needs it makes and keeps itself
Every operation works as the interface says
One person's items are never visible to or changeable by another
Accounts and items persist across restarts, and signing in still works after one
Invalid input is refused without storing anything
User registration and authentication (JWT-based)
Create, read, update, delete tasks
Assign tasks to team members
Set priorities (low, medium, high, urgent)
Due dates and reminders
Task categories and tags
Search and filter functionality
Users can register, login, logout securely
Task CRUD operations work correctly
Team collaboration features function properly
Analytics dashboard shows task statistics
API documentation available (Swagger/OpenAPI)
All endpoints have proper error handling
User Interface: Modern web application with responsive design
Database migrations required
Docker containerization
Count the words, lines and characters in a text file
List the most frequent words
Print the results as JSON for other programs
Read standard input when the file is given as -
Report a missing file as an error
Run as python -m wordstats <file> from the project directory. It prints three lines: words: <n>, lines: <n> and characters: <n>
A word is a run of letters, digits and apostrophes. characters counts every character, newlines included. lines is the number of lines; a last line without a newline still counts
--top N prints the N most frequent words instead, one per line as <word> <count>, most frequent first, ties in alphabetical order. Words are compared in lower case
--json prints {"words": n, "lines": n, "characters": n}, or with --top N prints {"top": [{"word": w, "count": c}, ...]}
A file that does not exist prints an error to standard error and exits with status 2
Counts are exactly as the interface defines them
The top words are ordered as the interface says
JSON output parses and matches the plain output
Errors go to standard error with exit status 2
Save a bookmark with a title, a URL and an optional tag
List saved bookmarks, newest first
Delete a bookmark
Filter the list by tag
Bookmarks are kept by the service and survive a reload of the page
The service serves the page at /
The page has a text field labelled "Title", a text field labelled "URL", a text field labelled "Tag" and a button named "Save bookmark"
A bookmark without a title, or whose URL does not start with http:// or https://, is not saved
Each bookmark is an item of a list showing its title as a link to its URL, and its tag. Each has a button named "Delete"
A text field labelled "Filter by tag" shows only the bookmarks with exactly that tag; when it is empty, all are shown
GET /api/bookmarks answers 200 with an array of {"id", "title", "url", "tag"}, newest first
POST /api/bookmarks with {"title", "url", "tag"} answers 201 with the bookmark, or 400 or 422 for invalid input, storing nothing
DELETE /api/bookmarks/{id} answers 204, or 404 when there is no such bookmark
The project directory has a start.sh that starts the service on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the PORT environment variable, keeping its data under the directory in DATA_DIR
Bookmarks can be saved, listed, filtered and deleted from the page
The JSON interface behaves as described
Invalid bookmarks are refused
The list survives a reload

interface_contract: AC-1 POST /api/bookmarks -> 400 {"error": "URL must start with http:// or https://"}

criteria.text: Create a note with a title and a body
List all notes
Fetch one note by its id
Update a note's title and body
Delete a note
Notes survive a restart of the service
JSON over HTTP. A note is {"id": <integer>, "title": <string>, "body": <string>}
POST /notes with {"title": ..., "body": ...} creates a note and answers 201 with the note
GET /notes answers 200 with a JSON array of every note
GET /notes/{id} answers 200 with the note, or 404 when there is none
PUT /notes/{id} with {"title": ..., "body": ...} replaces both and answers 200 with the note, or 404
DELETE /notes/{id} answers 204, or 404
A title that is missing or empty is refused with 400 or 422, and nothing is stored
GET /health answers 200
The project directory has a start.sh that starts the service on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the PORT environment variable, keeping its data under the directory in the DATA_DIR environment variable
Every operation works as the interface says
Notes persist across restarts
Invalid input is refused without storing anything
